authority: Official Steinberg Cubase Pro 15.0 English manual; documented behavior, not runtime observations of build 15.0.30.287

sources.title: Ruler Time Format Menu
claims: Bars+Beats displays bars, beats, sixteenths and ticks.
Default display resolution is 120 ticks per sixteenth and is configurable in MIDI preferences.
This display resolution is not proof of internal project storage resolution.

sources.title: Snap Types
claims: Grid Relative preserves an existing moved event's position relative to grid boundaries.
The documented Bar-grid example moves 3.04.01 to 4.04.01 or 5.04.01.
Creating a new event under Grid Relative uses ordinary Grid behavior.

sources.title: Grid
claims: Bars+Beats offers Bar, Beat, Use Quantize and Adapt to Zoom grids.
Time-based ruler formats use their corresponding time positions.

sources.title: Tempo Track Editor Toolbar
claims: Ramp changes gradually from the preceding point to the new point; Step changes instantly.
Time signature events snap to bar starts.
The page does not specify whether ramp interpolation is linear in elapsed seconds, quarter-note beats, or another domain.

sources.title: Signature Track Inspector
claims: Signature events have a bar position and a signature value.
The first signature event is fixed at bar 1.

sources.title: Track Time Base
claims: Musical time-base tracks follow tempo-track changes; linear time-base tracks use absolute time.
For audio events with musical time base, tempo changes affect their start position, not the audio itself.

sources.title: Defining the Track Time Base
claims: Musical positioning uses bars/beats while linear positioning uses elapsed time.
The manual warns that repeated conversion between the two bases loses some positioning precision.

not_established: Native floating-point operation order and internal PPQ
Ramp interpolation domain or exact inverse
Grid-relative behavior across a time-signature change
Sample-accurate tempo-event evaluation and MIDI serialization
